court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Vishal Laxmanrao Gadewar And 3 Others vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. Pso Ps ...

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Maharashtra, through P.S.O. Police Station Yavatmal City, Yavatmal & Anr.

facts_of_case: Matrimonial dispute between applicant No.1 and non-applicant No.2; FIR registered for offence under Section 498-A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code; parties settled their mutual dispute and decided to put an end to all litigations.

legal_principles.principle: FIRs of such nature arising from matrimonial disputes can be quashed by the High Court if parties mutually settle their disputes.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012(10) SC 303, has held that FIRs of such nature arising from matrimonial disputes can be quashed by the High Court by exercising power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.,
cited_cases: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another, (2012) 10 SCC 303
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — in cases where parties settle their disputes

outcome.final_order: The investigation may go on, but the charge-sheet shall not be filed without the leave of this Court.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
use_for_drafting: drafting a quashing petition for a criminal case
advising on the applicability of Section 498-A IPC
assisting in a divorce matter involving allegations of domestic violence
